transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I'm just so tired all the time, and I've no energy for anything. It's got to the point where I'm napping most days, which I never used to do.
Can you tell me a bit more about when this tiredness first started, how it came on, and whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
Since last week, I'd say. And yes — codeine makes me terribly sick, I can't take it at all.
Could you tell me how this tiredness is affecting your daily life, and what medicines you are currently taking, including any new or changed ones?

I've had to give up my swimming twice a week, and I'm struggling to help my husband wash and dress in the mornings — my energy's only about 3 out of 10. As for medicines, I take metformin 500 mg twice a day, levothyroxine 100 micrograms each morning, omeprazole 20 mg once a day for my indigestion, and I buy ibuprofen 400 mg from the chemist and take those most days for my shoulder.
Could you tell me about any health problems, illnesses, or operations you've had in the past, and whether you've noticed anything else going on alongside the tiredness?
I've had type 2 diabetes for about 12 years and an underactive thyroid. Besides the tiredness, I get more short of breath than usual going up hills, and a couple of friends have said I look pale.
When you feel this tiredness, does it seem to be all over your body, or is it more in one particular part?
It's not in any one place — it's just a general tiredness all over, really. I haven't noticed it being worse in any particular part of my body.
What sorts of things seem to make your tiredness better or worse?
It's fairly steady all day, but I'd say it's worse in the afternoon — that's when I really need that nap. I can't say I've found anything that makes it much better.
Is there anything else you’d like to add about any medicines you take, including anything you’ve bought or started recently?
No, I don't think so — the ibuprofen is the only thing I buy myself, and that's been going on a while. I haven't started anything new.
What worries you most about your tiredness, and what are you hoping we can do for you today?
My biggest worry is that I won't be able to keep looking after my husband — he's got Parkinson's and needs a lot of help. I'm hoping we can find out what's causing this and get me back on my feet.
Apart from the diabetes and underactive thyroid you mentioned, is there anything else about your past health, such as other conditions, operations, or hospital stays, that you’d like to add?
No, nothing else that I can think of — it's just the diabetes and the thyroid.
Could you describe what the tiredness feels like for you, in your own words?
It's like a heavy, draining feeling — I just don't have any get-up-and-go, and everything feels like a lot of effort. Even after a sleep I still wake up feeling unrefreshed.
Besides getting short of breath going up hills and your friends saying you look pale, is there anything else you’d like to add about how you’ve been feeling?

My sleep isn't great — I get about seven hours but I wake up not feeling refreshed. And if I'm honest, my mood feels a bit flat, what with all the caring. No chest pain though, and my weight and bowels have been fine.
Is there anything else you'd like to add?
No, I think that's everything. I just want to get to the bottom of why I'm so tired.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
